name: company_invitations
description: An invitation for a recipient address to join a company with one grant; only the person signed in with that verified address can accept it.
lifecycle: Created PENDING with a seven-day validity; becomes ACCEPTED, REVOKED by an inviter, REPLACED by a resend or EXPIRED. The recipient address is replaced by a tombstone (NULL) 90 days after the invitation becomes final (provisional until PH-13); the row and its audit events remain.

columns.Meaning: Company the invitation admits to; immutable (tenant key).
Trimmed, lower-cased recipient address the accepting identity's verified email must equal.
columns.Null meaning: The invitation is final and its retention period ended, so the address was erased.

columns.Meaning: SHA-256 hash of the invitation's 256-bit credential; the credential itself is never stored in plaintext.
Standard role the accepted invitation grants.
COMPANY or explicit BRANCHES listed in company_invitation_branches; administration is always company-wide.
Expiry of the granted access once accepted; never renewed automatically (P30).
columns.Null meaning: The granted access does not expire.

columns.Meaning: Membership of the inviter, whose authority is rechecked at acceptance.
PENDING until accepted, revoked, replaced or expired.
Outbound email that carries the invitation, owned by the mail module; a soft reference, because the mail module deletes final messages after their retention period.
Pending invitation this one replaced through a resend.
columns.Null meaning: The invitation was not created by a resend.

columns.Meaning: Membership that received the invited grant on acceptance.
PostgreSQL-clock instant the invitation was created.
Instant after which the pending invitation can no longer be accepted.
PostgreSQL-clock instant the invitation stopped being pending.

constraints.Purpose: Exactly the accepted invitations name the membership that received the grant.

constraints.Physical definition: FOREIGN KEY (company_id, accepted_membership_id) REFERENCES memberships(company_id, id) ON UPDATE RESTRICT ON DELETE RESTRICT
constraints.Purpose: The accepting membership belongs to the same company.

constraints.Physical definition: FOREIGN KEY (company_id) REFERENCES companies(id) ON UPDATE RESTRICT ON DELETE RESTRICT
constraints.Purpose: An invitation belongs to an existing company.

constraints.Physical definition: FOREIGN KEY (company_id, invited_by_membership_id) REFERENCES memberships(company_id, id) ON UPDATE RESTRICT ON DELETE RESTRICT
constraints.Purpose: The inviter is a membership of the same company.

constraints.Physical definition: FOREIGN KEY (company_id, replaces_invitation_id) REFERENCES company_invitations(company_id, id) ON UPDATE RESTRICT ON DELETE RESTRICT
constraints.Purpose: A resend replaces an invitation of the same company.
The stored credential hash is a SHA-256 digest.
A decision instant exists exactly for invitations that are no longer pending.
An invitation expires after it was created.
A temporary grant ends after the invitation was created.
A pending invitation always has its recipient address.
Recipient addresses are stored trimmed and lower-cased.

constraints.Physical definition: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX company_invitations_company_id_id_key ON public.company_invitations USING btree (company_id, id)
constraints.Purpose: Tenant key for references to invitations.

constraints.Physical definition: CREATE INDEX company_invitations_company_time_idx ON public.company_invitations USING btree (company_id, created_at DESC, id DESC)
constraints.Purpose: Lists a company's invitations newest first with stable keyset pagination.

constraints.Physical definition: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX company_invitations_credential_key ON public.company_invitations USING btree (credential_hash)
constraints.Purpose: Finds an invitation by credential hash; credentials never collide.

constraints.Physical definition: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX company_invitations_one_pending ON public.company_invitations USING btree (company_id, recipient_email) WHERE (status = 'PENDING'::"InvitationStatus")
constraints.Purpose: At most one pending invitation per company and address, including racing requests.

constraints.Physical definition: CREATE INDEX company_invitations_recipient_idx ON public.company_invitations USING btree (recipient_email, created_at)
constraints.Purpose: Counts recent invitations to one address across companies for the abuse limit.
